chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'During the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the Mercy of his Lord.' He said: 'It means the night prayer.'
I said to him, 'And the parts of the day, so that you may be well pleased.' He said: 'It means performing voluntary prayer during the day.'
I said to him, 'And the retreat of the stars.' He said: 'Two Rak'at before the morning prayer.'
I said, 'And after the prostrations.' He said: 'Two Rak'at after the Maghrib prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times and forms of voluntary prayer mentioned in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Quranic temporal markers for voluntary worship, linking specific verses to distinct prayer times. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating night devotion (Qiyam al-Layl) with daytime sunnah prayers, specifically identifying the two Rak'at before Fajr and after Maghrib as key moments of spiritual connection.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘[39:9] Safe is He who is obedient during the hours of the night, performing Sajdah himself and standing, cautious of the Hereafter and hopes for the Mercy of his Lord’. Heasws said: ‘It Means the night Salāt’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to himasws [20:130] so Glorify (Him) during parts of the day, so that you may be well pleased’. Heasws said: ‘It Means the voluntary (Salāt) at daytime’. He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘[52:49] and (Glorify Him) at the retreat of the stars’. Heasws said: ‘Two Rak’at prayed before the morning’. I said, ‘[50:40] so glorify Him and after the Sajdahs?’ Heasws said: ‘Two Rak’at after Al-Maghrib’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, ‘. . . during the night in Sajdah (prostration) and in standing position fearful of the next life and hopeful of the mercy of his Lord. . . .’ [20:130]. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a reference to the nightly optional Salah (prayer).’
I then said, ‘ . . . and in both ends of the day perhaps you will become happy. . .’ [20:130]. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a reference to optional Salah (prayer) during the day.’
I then said, ‘. . . when the stars go back. . . .’ [52:49]. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a reference to the two Rak‘at before the morning Salah (prayer).’
I then said, ‘. . . after Sujud (prostrations) . . .’[52:40] He (the Imam) said, ‘It is a reference to the two Rak‘at after al-Maghrib.’”
